session.about: Manage chat sessions: create, send, open, list, get, rename, move, clear project, fork, archive

create.about: Create a new chat session and send a prompt in it (fire-and-forget)
create.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session create --prompt "Triage the failing nightly build" \
    --harness-id claude-acp --json

Result:
  {"session_id": "...", "title": "...", "harness_id": "...",
   "send_status": "dispatched"}
  The session runs in the background; the user's view does not change. Check
  progress later with `berdctl session get --session-id <session_id>`.

send.about: Send a prompt into an existing chat session
send.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session send --session-id <session-id> \
    --prompt "Check the latest CI failure" --if-running queue --json

Result:
  {"session_id": "...", "send_status": "dispatched"|"steered"|"queued"}
  The user's current view does not change.

open.about: Open a session in the app window the user is looking at
open.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session open --session-id <session-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the session is now on screen.

list.about: List the user's chat sessions (most recent first)
list.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session list --query "review" --limit 10 --json

Result:
  {"sessions": [{"session_id": "...", "title": "...",
                 "project_id": "..."|null, "updated_at": "...",
                 "message_count": 12}, ...]}
  Most recent first; archived sessions are excluded.

get.about: Read one session's metadata and optionally its latest messages
get.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session get --session-id <session-id> --messages 5 --json

Result:
  {"session_id": "...", "title": "...", "harness_id": "...",
   "model_id": "..."|null, "agent_id": "..."|null,
   "project_id": "..."|null, "working_dir": "..."|null,
   "created_at": "...", "updated_at": "...", "archived": false,
   "message_count": 12,
   "messages": [{"role": "user"|"assistant"|null, "text": "..."}, ...]}
  "messages" is present only when --messages > 0; each message text is
  truncated to 2000 chars.

rename.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session rename --session-id <session-id> --title "CI triage"

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the new title appears immediately in the app's session list.

move.about: Move a chat session into a project
move.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session move --session-id <session-id> --project-id <project-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the app's session list regroups immediately.

clear-project.about: Move a chat session out of any project
clear-project.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session clear-project --session-id <session-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the app's session list regroups immediately.

fork.about: Fork a chat session into an independent copy with its history
fork.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl session fork --session-id <session-id> --title "Alternate approach"

Result:
  {"session_id": "...", "title": "...", "source_session_id": "...",
   "message_count": 7}
  The fork appears in the session list with a copy of the original history.

archive.about: Archive a chat session (reversible; nothing is deleted)
archive.afterHelp:
Archiving is reversible from the app's archive view; nothing is deleted.

Example:
  berdctl session archive --session-id <session-id>

  Result:
  {"ok": true} — the session disappears from the active session list.

project.about: Manage projects: create, list, get, archive

create.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl project create --name "Code reviews" \
    --instructions "Prefer small diffs" --working-dir /Users/me/src/repo

Result:
  {"project_id": "..."} — the project appears immediately in the app's
  project list.

get.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl project get --project-id <project-id> --json

Result:
  {"project_id": "...", "name": "...", "description": "...",
   "instructions": "...", "working_dirs": ["..."], "archived": false,
   "session_count": 4}

archive.about: Archive a project (reversible; nothing is deleted)
archive.afterHelp:
Archiving is reversible from the app's archive view; nothing is
deleted, and the project's sessions are left untouched.

Example:
  berdctl project archive --project-id <project-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the project disappears from the app's project list.

create.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl agent create --name "Reviewer" \
    --system-prompt "You review diffs for correctness; be terse."

Result:
  {"agent_id": "..."} — the agent is saved and becomes available in
  future chats; pass it as --agent-id to `berdctl session create`.

list.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl agent list --json

Result:
  {"agents": [{"agent_id": "...", "name": "...",
               "summary": "...", "builtin": false}, ...]}
  Use an agent_id as --agent-id when creating a session.

create.about: Create a new skill (saved as a SKILL.md)
create.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl skill create --name "release-notes" \
    --description "Draft release notes from merged PRs" \
    --content "$(cat SKILL.md)"

Result:
  {"skill_id": "..."} — the skill is saved as a SKILL.md and auto-loads
  into future sessions.

list.about: List the user's skills (name and description only)
list.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl skill list --json

Result:
  {"skills": [{"skill_id": "...", "name": "...",
               "description": "...",
               "source": "builtin"|"global"|"project"}, ...]}
  Read a skill's full content with `berdctl skill get`.

get.about: Read one skill including its SKILL.md instructions

info.about: Look up installed harnesses, available models, and the app context

harnesses.about: List the agent harnesses sessions can run on, with readiness
harnesses.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl info harnesses --json

Result:
  {"harnesses": [{"harness_id": "goose", "name": "...",
                  "is_default": true,
                  "status": "ready"|"not_installed"|"not_ready"}, ...]}
  Only "ready" harnesses accept new sessions; "not_installed" and
  "not_ready" (sign-in or setup required) need the user to fix them in
  the app first.

models.about: List the models available per agent harness
models.afterHelp:
Example:
  berdctl info models --harness-id goose --json

Result:
  {"harnesses": [{"harness_id": "...",
                  "models": [{"model_id": "...", "name": "...",
                              "provider": "..."?}],
                  "warning": "..."?}]}
  Use a model_id (with its harness) as --model-id when creating a session.
  "warning" appears when a stale cached list was served or when the harness
  manages its model outside the app.

context.about: Read what the user is looking at in the app right now
